chapter: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
title: Playing 'Blue Bells of Scotland' from the troop ship
summary: Arriving at Greenock, he plays the song his mother taught him, bagpipes answer and the colonel restores his sergeant's stripes; he plays it again.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What is it, there's a story that I've read you might want to authenticate it if it can be authenticated, that when you arrived on the troop ship in Scotland which by the way was your mother's home to begin with, that you created such a sensation before ever getting off the boat. As a matter of fact, I think the troops could hardly get off the boat because you started playing kind of a hot
On the Benge horn. With the Benge horn, yes.

We got to Scotland on this troop ship and I thought well my gosh, my mother was, it was Greenock we landed and my gosh here's my mother's home near Glasgow. And when I was younger, rather when I first started to play the cornet my mother asked me one day, she said to me she said, James, when I was in the choir in Scotland why I used to sing alto. And she said one of the songs that we used to sing all the time was 'Blue Bells of Scotland'. Oh where tell me where is my Island laddie now. So I thought and my mother was dead already so I thought well this would be the time for me to get out the horn and say hello to mama.

And she taught me how to play 'Blue Bells of Scotland' and so I figured I'll blow the thing. And I did, I played 'Blue Bells of Scotland' the first chorus real straight and pretty and then I jazzed it up in the second chorus.
Well I think you ought to do it

Alright I'll try. I'll blow a few notes here and get my chops warmed up. I'll try it. But the thing that happened Helen was it was so beautiful, it was so quiet in this bay that man as soon as I blew this 'Blue Bells of Scotland' well all the bagpipes started going on shore and everything. And the people all started hollering. You could hear them all that distance, quite a distance.
And we got in, the colonel man, he said, great stuff McPartland you know. Cementing relations with our allies style, so he made me a sergeant again. (LAUGHTER).
I had been busted, yes. (LAUGHTER). Sure. So I don't know, I'll play, I'll try to play. I'm not too warmed up but I'll try to play it like I played it then and see what happens.
Otherwise only the people who were there that day know what this was all about. Now a lot of people can know.
('BLUE BELLS OF SCOTLAND' IS PLAYED ON CORNET BY MR. McPARTLAND)....................................
Oh that's, and the State Irish, I mean the State Scotch at that? Oh no wonder.

Well I told you, I had been busted I came back late from my leave before we left and I was a Buck Sergeant before we left America and they busted me quick. Or else Court-Martial me and I decided to get busted.
So that was that and so the colonel, cementing relations made me a sergeant again.
